chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Bill Robinson and Louis Armstrong as deep thinkers
summary: McRae finds both men gentle, thoughtful behind their showman faces.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: That's the kind of guy. He was -- just like nothing. Louie was more like Bill Robinson than anybody I worked with. Now there's a man with a beautiful mind, Bill Robinson. You never know -- See, it's a funny thing about a person. You never know them till you work with them. Bill Robinson was a great man. Had a great, great mind. All of -- (inaudible) he was the most educated man in the world (inaudible) -- schooling he had in his life. But he had a great sense of humor. Great (inaudible), you know. And he was a great man. You be behind closed doors with him, he
